lines.text: For the choirmaster: To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Psalm of Asaph. A song.
We give thanks to You, O God;
we give thanks, for Your Name is near.
The people declare Your wondrous works.
When the earth and all its dwellers quake,
it is I who bear up its pillars.
I say to the proud, ‘Do not boast,’
and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn.
Do not lift up your horn against heaven
or speak with an outstretched neck.’”

pictures.scene: Cornelis Pietersz Bega, Het gebed voor de maaltijd — the household stopped with heads bowed over the table before they eat, for the choirmaster to the tune of Do Not Destroy a Psalm of Asaph a song, we give thanks to You O God
pictures.name: pd_bega_gebed_voor_de_maaltijd

pictures.scene: Teodor Axentowicz, Feast of Jordan — the whole village crowded down to the river for the blessing of the water, we give thanks for Your Name is near, the people declare Your wondrous works
pictures.name: pd_axentowicz_feast_of_jordan

pictures.scene: Werner van den Valckert, Four Regents of the Groot-Kramergild — the appointed men seated at the table with the book open to give their ruling, when I choose a time I will judge fairly
pictures.name: pd_valckert_regents_kramergild

pictures.scene: Louwrens Hanedoes and Herman Frederik Carel ten Kate, Berglandschap met ruïne — the broken walls standing on the rock above the valley, when the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars
pictures.name: pd_hanedoes_berglandschap_met_ruine

pictures.scene: Pontormo, Portrait of a Halberdier — the young man standing very straight with his weapon and his hand on his hip, Selah, I say to the proud do not boast
pictures.name: pd_pontormo_halberdier

pictures.scene: Raphael, The Meeting of Leo the Great and Attila — the raider's advance stopped in the road by the one who came out to meet him, and to the wicked do not lift up your horn, do not lift up your horn against heaven
pictures.name: pd_raphael_leo_attila

pictures.scene: Cornelius van Poelenburgh, Italianiserend landschap met een oudtestamentisch onderwerp — the men standing in the open country arguing it out with a finger raised, or speak with an outstretched neck, for exaltation comes neither from east nor west
pictures.name: pd_poelenburgh_italianiserend_landschap
